cando: I can start a conversation, keep it going and end it politely.
I can give my opinion with reasons, agree and disagree politely, and ask what someone means.
I can talk about my experiences, tell a story, explain a problem and describe my hopes for the future.
cando_ar: أستطيع أن أبدأ محادثة وأواصلها وأنهيها بلطف.
أستطيع أن أعبّر عن رأيي مع ذكر الأسباب، وأوافق وأخالف بأدب، وأسأل عمّا يقصده الآخرون.
أستطيع أن أتحدث عن تجاربي، وأروي قصة، وأشرح مشكلة، وأصف آمالي للمستقبل.

cards.q: Hi! I haven't seen you in a long time. How have you been?
cards.simple: Hi! It's been a long time. How are you?
a: I've been really busy because we had exams all month. It's so good to see you!
I've been great, thanks! We moved to a new house, so I've been unpacking boxes all week.
useful: It's so good to see you!
cards.ask: Greet a friend you haven't seen in a long time, and ask how she has been.

cards.q: Hi! Is this your first day at the summer program?
cards.simple: Hi! Are you new here at the summer program?
a: Yes, it's my first day, so I don't know anyone yet. What about you?
No, it's my second year. I came back because I loved the robotics workshop last year.
cards.ask: Start a conversation with a girl at a summer program. Ask her if it's her first day.

cards.q: Do you want to stay and have another coffee?
cards.simple: Can you stay a little longer?
a: I'd love to, but I'd better go because my mom is waiting outside. It was so nice talking to you!
Sorry, I can't, because I have a test tomorrow. Let's catch up on the weekend!
useful: It was so nice talking to you!
cards.ask: Ask your friend if she wants to stay and have another coffee.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: you meet an old friend at the mall.
cards.simple: You see an old friend at the mall. Say hello, talk a little, and then say goodbye.
steps: Greet her and say how long it has been.
Tell her one piece of news.
Say you have to go, and give a reason.
Say goodbye and suggest meeting again.
a: Hi! Wow, I haven't seen you in two years!
How have you been?
I've moved to a new school this year, and I really like it.
I'm sorry, but I'd better go because my sister is waiting for me.
It was so nice to see you. Let's catch up soon!

cards.q: Have you ever been to AlUla?
cards.simple: Did you ever visit AlUla?
a: Yes, I have! I went there last winter with my family, and I loved it because the rocks look amazing at sunset.
No, I haven't, but I'd really like to go. My cousin says it's beautiful, so maybe we'll go next winter.
cards.ask: Ask your friend if she has ever been to AlUla.

cards.q: Have you ever tried a food that you didn't like?
cards.simple: Did you ever eat something new and not like it?
a: Yes, I have. I tried sushi once, but I didn't like it because the fish was raw.
Not really, because I love trying new food. Last month, I had Korean food for the first time, and it was delicious!
cards.ask: Ask your friend if she has ever tried a food that she didn't like.

cards.q: What's the most exciting thing you've ever done?
cards.simple: What is the most exciting thing you did in your life?
a: I once gave a speech in front of the whole school. I was nervous, but I felt so proud because everyone clapped.
I've been snorkeling in the Red Sea with my family. It was amazing because I saw so many colorful fish.
cards.ask: Ask your friend about the most exciting thing she has ever done.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: describe a place you have visited.
cards.simple: Talk about a trip: where you went, what you did and how it was.
steps: Say when you went and who you went with.
Say how you felt and why.
Say if you would like to go again.
a: I've been to Abha.
I went there two summers ago with my family.
We walked in the mountains and visited the old markets.
I loved it because it was cool and green.
I'd love to go again next summer.

cards.q: What would you like to study at university, and why?
cards.simple: What do you want to study after school?
a: I'd like to study medicine because I want to help people. My aunt is a doctor, and she's my role model.
I'm hoping to study computer science. I've always loved solving problems, so I think it's perfect for me.
cards.ask: Ask your friend what she would like to study at university, and why.

cards.q: Where do you see yourself in ten years?
cards.simple: What will your life be like in ten years?
a: I hope I'll be working as an engineer on a big national project. I'd love that because I want to help build my country.
In ten years, I'd like to have my own business. I love design, so I might open a small studio.
useful: In ten years, I'd like to ...
cards.ask: Ask your friend where she sees herself in ten years.

cards.q: What might stop you from reaching your goal?
cards.simple: What problems could you have?
a: Medicine is a long degree, so I'll need to be patient. But I'm ready to work hard.
My English isn't strong enough yet, so I'm practicing every day. I read English books because they help me a lot.
cards.ask: Ask your friend what might stop her from reaching her goal.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: tell a friend about your dream.
cards.simple: Talk about your dream: what it is, why, and what you are doing now.
steps: Explain why it matters to you.
Say one step you are taking now.
Say one problem you might have and what you will do.
a: My dream is to become a pharmacist.
It matters to me because my grandmother takes a lot of medicine, and I want to help people like her.
Right now, I'm working hard in chemistry and biology.
It might be hard to get into a good university, so I'm going to start preparing early.

cards.q: I think online classes are better than classes at school. What do you think?
cards.simple: Do you like online classes more than school classes?
a: I see what you mean, but I'm not sure about that. I learn better at school because I can ask the teacher questions face to face.
I agree with you, because you save a lot of time at home. But I'd really miss my friends!
useful: I see what you mean, but ...
cards.ask: Tell your friend you think online classes are better than classes at school, and ask what she thinks.

cards.q: Social media is a waste of time, don't you think?
cards.simple: Do you think social media wastes our time?
a: That's true for some people, but it depends on how you use it. I follow science accounts, so I learn a lot.
You're right. I spend too much time on it, so I'm trying to use it less.
useful: That's true for some people, but ...
cards.ask: Tell your friend you think social media is a waste of time, and ask if she agrees.

cards.q: I think everyone should learn coding at school.
cards.simple: Should all students learn coding?
a: I totally agree, because coding is useful in so many jobs. It also teaches you to solve problems step by step.
I'm not so sure. Coding is great, but some students prefer art or languages, so it should be a choice.
cards.ask: Tell your friend you think everyone should learn coding at school.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: your friend wants a class trip to the mall. You prefer the science museum.
cards.simple: Your friend wants to go to the mall. You want to go to the museum. Say why, in a kind way.
steps: Say something nice about her idea.
Suggest a way to make everyone happy.
a: That's a fun idea.
But I'm not sure the mall is the best place for a class trip.
I think we should go to the science museum.
There's a new space exhibition, so we can learn something new.
How about the museum in the morning and lunch at the mall after?

cards.q: For your project, please cite at least three sources.
cards.simple: In your project, write the names of three books or websites you used.
a: Sorry, what do you mean by "cite"? I've never heard that word, so I'm not sure what to do.
Could you give us an example, please? I'm asking because I want to do it the right way.
useful: Sorry, what do you mean by ...?
Could you give us an example?
cards.ask: You are the teacher. Tell the class to cite at least three sources for their project.

cards.q: The club meeting has moved to Tuesday, in Room 12, right after the break.
cards.simple: The club meeting is now on Tuesday after the break, in Room 12.
a: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you say it again more slowly, so I can write it down?
So the meeting is on Tuesday, right after the break? I'm just checking because I don't want to miss it.
useful: Could you say it again more slowly?
cards.ask: Tell your friend the club meeting has moved to Tuesday, in Room 12, right after the break.

cards.q: Don't worry, the test is going to be a piece of cake!
cards.simple: Don't worry, the test will be very easy!
a: Sorry, what does "a piece of cake" mean? I don't get it, because we aren't talking about food!
Do you mean it's going to be easy? I hope you're right, because I'm really worried!
cards.ask: Tell your worried friend that the test is going to be a piece of cake.

cards.q: Your teacher explains the homework too fast. Ask her to help you understand.
cards.simple: The teacher speaks too fast. Ask her to say it again and explain.
steps: Ask her to say it again more slowly.
a: Sorry, Ms. ___, I didn't quite understand.
Could you say that again more slowly, please?
What do you mean by "summarize"?
So we have to write the main ideas in five lines?
That's clear now. Thank you so much!

cards.q: What happened? You look so excited!
cards.simple: Why are you so happy? Tell me what happened.
a: I was checking my email when I saw the news. I got into the coding camp I applied for, so I can't stop smiling!
My little sister said her first English word this morning! We were having breakfast when she suddenly said "apple," so we all laughed.
cards.ask: Your friend looks very excited. Ask her what happened.

cards.q: Has anything funny happened to you this week?
cards.simple: Did something funny happen to you this week?
a: Yes! I was making tea for my mom's guests when I put salt in it instead of sugar. Nobody said anything because they were too polite!
Yes! My mom was looking for her glasses all morning, so we all helped her. Then my sister noticed they were on her head the whole time!
cards.ask: Ask your friend if anything funny has happened to her this week.

cards.q: How was your trip? I heard your flight was late.
cards.simple: Was your trip good? Was your plane late?
a: It was a long day! We waited at the airport for six hours, so we were exhausted when we finally arrived.
It was fine in the end. The flight was late, but we met our cousins at the airport, so we didn't get bored.
cards.ask: Your friend's flight was late. Ask her how her trip was.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: tell a story about a day when something went wrong.
cards.simple: Tell a story about a bad day: what happened and how it ended.
a: It happened last Ramadan.
I was helping my mom make iftar for the whole family.
Suddenly, the power went out just before sunset.
So we lit some candles and ate in the garden.
In the end, it was the best iftar ever because it felt like a picnic.

cards.q: So you'd like to return this? What's wrong with it?
cards.simple: Why do you want to give it back?
a: It stopped working after two days. I've only used it twice, so I'd like to exchange it, please.
The screen is cracked, but I didn't drop it. I think it was broken in the box, so could I get a refund?
cards.ask: You work in a store. A customer wants to return something. Ask her what's wrong with it.

cards.q: Is everything OK with your meal?
cards.simple: Do you like your food?
a: Not really, I'm afraid. My pasta is cold, so could you heat it up, please?
The food is great, thank you. But we've been waiting for our drinks for twenty minutes, so could you check on them?
useful: Could you heat it up, please?
cards.ask: You are the waiter. Ask the customer if everything is OK with her meal.

cards.q: Thank you for calling customer service. How can I help you?
cards.simple: Hello, this is the store. What is the problem?
a: I ordered a blue dress online, but you sent a green one. I need it for my cousin's wedding on Thursday, so could you send the right one quickly?
My order was supposed to arrive three days ago, but it still hasn't come. It's a gift for my mom's birthday, so I really need it by Saturday.
cards.ask: You work in customer service. Answer the phone and ask how you can help.

cards.q: Your new laptop stopped working. Call the store and make a complaint.
cards.simple: Your laptop is broken. Call the store. Say what is wrong and what you want.
steps: Say what you bought and when.
Say what you have already tried.
Explain why it is a big problem for you.
Say what you want them to do.
a: Hello, I bought a laptop from your store two weeks ago.
It turns off by itself every few minutes.
I've already restarted it many times, but it still doesn't work.
I'm a student, so I need it for my homework every day.
Could you fix it quickly or give me a new one, please?

cards.q: What seems to be the problem?
cards.simple: What is wrong? How do you feel?
a: I've had a bad headache for three days. I can't sleep well, so I feel tired all the time.
I have a sore throat and a fever. It started yesterday, so I stayed home from school today.
cards.ask: You are the doctor. Ask your patient what the problem is.

cards.q: Your ankle looks swollen. How did it happen?
cards.simple: Your ankle is bigger than normal. What happened?
a: I was playing basketball at school, and I fell. It hurts when I walk, so my mom brought me here.
I'm not really sure, because I didn't fall. It started hurting after a long walk yesterday.
cards.ask: You are the doctor. Tell your patient her ankle looks swollen, and ask how it happened.

cards.q: You should rest for a few days and drink lots of water.
cards.simple: Stay home, rest and drink a lot of water.
a: OK, thank you. I have an important test on Wednesday, so can I still go to school?
Thank you, Doctor. Should I take something for the pain? It's hard to sleep because it hurts at night.
cards.ask: You are the doctor. Tell your patient she should rest for a few days and drink lots of water.

cards.q: You have a stomachache. Tell the doctor about it.
cards.simple: Tell the doctor what is wrong and since when. Then ask what to do.
steps: Say how long you have had it.
Say what you have already tried.
a: I have a terrible stomachache.
I've had it since Monday.
It gets worse after I eat, so I'm not eating much.
I tried some mint tea, but it didn't help.
What should I do, Doctor?

cards.q: Can you teach me how to make Saudi coffee?
cards.simple: How do you make Saudi coffee?
a: Sure! First, you boil the coffee in water for about ten minutes. Then you add the cardamom and let it rest, so the coffee goes to the bottom.
Of course! The secret is the cardamom, so don't be shy with it. My grandmother also adds a little saffron because it gives a beautiful color.
cards.ask: Ask your friend to teach you how to make Saudi coffee.

cards.q: How do I send a voice message on my phone?
cards.simple: Can you show me how to send a voice message?
a: It's easy, so don't worry! Just hold the microphone button while you talk, and let go when you finish.
First, open the chat. Then hold the microphone button and don't let go until you finish, because it sends as soon as you let go.
cards.ask: Ask your friend how to send a voice message on your phone.

cards.q: What's the best way to study for a big test?
cards.simple: How do you study for an important test?
a: I always make a study plan first, so I don't leave everything until the last minute. Then I study for an hour and take a short break.
Try teaching the lesson to someone else, because it shows you what you don't understand. It really works for me!
cards.ask: Ask your friend for the best way to study for a big test.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: explain how to make a drink you love.
cards.simple: Say how to make a drink you like, step by step.
a: To make karak tea, you need black tea, milk, sugar and cardamom.
First, boil the tea and cardamom in water for a few minutes.
Then add the milk and sugar, and let it boil again.
Make sure you watch it, because milk can boil over very fast.
Finally, pour it into small cups and serve it hot.

cards.q: What are you reading right now?
cards.simple: Are you reading a book now? Which one?
a: I'm reading a mystery novel in English. It's a bit hard, but I can't stop reading because I want to know the ending!
Nothing right now, because I've been so busy with exams. But I've just bought a book about space, so I'll start it this weekend.
cards.ask: Ask your friend what she is reading right now.

cards.q: Have you watched any good documentaries lately?
cards.simple: Did you watch a good documentary recently?
a: Yes! I watched one about the ocean last week. I'd really recommend it because the animals are amazing.
Yes, I saw one about the history of Diriyah. I learned a lot, because I didn't know much about it before.
cards.ask: Ask your friend if she has watched any good documentaries lately.

cards.q: What did you think of the ending?
cards.simple: Did you like the end of the story?
a: I loved it, because I didn't expect it at all! The writer really surprised me.
Honestly, I was a bit disappointed. The story was great, but the ending was too fast, so I still have so many questions.
useful: I didn't expect it at all!
cards.ask: You and your friend watched the same series. Ask her what she thought of the ending.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: recommend a book or a series to a friend.
cards.simple: Tell your friend about a good book or series and why she should try it.
steps: Say the name of the book or series.
Say one thing you didn't like.
Say why your friend would enjoy it.
a: I'd recommend a novel called Wonder.
It's about a boy who looks different and goes to school for the first time.
What I liked most was how his family supported him.
The middle part was a bit slow, but it gets better.
I think you'd enjoy it because you love stories about friendship.

cards.q: What would you do if you had a million riyals?
cards.simple: Imagine you have a million riyals. How do you spend it?
a: I'd buy my parents a new house, because they've done so much for me. Then I'd save the rest for university.
If I had that much money, I'd give some to charity first. I'd also travel with my family, because I've always wanted to see Japan.
cards.ask: Ask your friend what she would do if she had a million riyals.

cards.q: If you could have any job for one day, what would it be?
cards.simple: Imagine you can do any job for one day. Which job do you choose?
a: I'd be an astronaut, because I'd love to see the Earth from space. Just one day would be enough for me!
I think I'd be a chef in a famous restaurant. I love cooking, so it would be like a dream.
useful: it would be like a dream
cards.ask: Ask your friend what job she would choose if she could have any job for one day.

cards.q: My best friend is upset with me, and I don't know why. What would you do?
cards.simple: My friend is angry with me. What should I do?
a: If I were you, I'd just ask her what's wrong. It might be a small problem, so it's better to talk about it.
I'd send her a kind message first, because she might not want to talk yet. Then I'd give her a little time.
cards.ask: Tell your friend that your best friend is upset with you and you don't know why. Ask her what she would do.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: what would you do if you were the principal of your school for a week?
cards.simple: Imagine you are the principal for one week. What do you change and why?
steps: Say the first thing you would change.
Say one new activity you would start.
Say one thing you wouldn't change.
Say how the students would feel.
a: First, I'd make the break longer.
Students need time to eat and rest, so they would focus better in class.
I'd also start a science club after school.
I wouldn't change the teachers, because they're great!
I think the students would be much happier.

cards.q: Why do you want to join our volunteering team?
cards.simple: Why do you want to be a volunteer with us?
a: I want to join because I love helping people. Last Ramadan, I helped pack food baskets, and it felt amazing.
I'm interested in this team because I want to give back to my community. It would also give me good experience for university.
useful: I want to give back to my community.
cards.ask: You are the team leader. Ask a new student why she wants to join your volunteering team.

cards.q: What skills can you bring to the club?
cards.simple: What are you good at? How can you help the club?
a: I'm good at organizing things, so I could help plan events. I'm also very good with computers.
I've designed posters for school events before, so I could help with the club's social media. I'm a good team player, too.
cards.ask: You are the club leader. Ask a new member what skills she can bring to the club.

cards.q: Members have to come every Tuesday after school. Is that OK for you?
cards.simple: You must come every Tuesday after school. Can you come?
a: Yes, that's fine, because I'm free on Tuesdays. Could I ask what time the meetings finish?
I might miss some Tuesdays, because I have extra classes before exams. Is that a problem?
cards.ask: You are the club leader. Tell a new member she has to come every Tuesday after school, and ask if that's OK.

cards.q: Talk for 30 seconds: introduce yourself at an interview to volunteer at a children's science day.
cards.simple: Tell the interviewer about you: why you want to help, what you did before and when you are free.
steps: Say why you want to volunteer.
a: My name is ___, and I'm in grade eleven.
I want to volunteer because I'd like to help children enjoy science.
Last year, I helped at a reading event for kids at the library.
I'm patient, and I can explain things clearly.
I'm free on weekends and most afternoons.
